title: Addon-Vitest: Make Playwright `--with-deps` platform-aware to avoid `sudo` prompt on Linux
body:
#### Manual testing

Create a sandbox on Linux. There should be no sudo prompt.

----
During `storybook init`, the addon-vitest postinstall was running `npx playwright install chromium --with-deps`, which triggers system-level package installation (apt/pacman/etc.) requiring `sudo` on Linux — prompting users for a root password mid-init with no clear context.

## Changes

- **`AddonVitestService.ts`**: Use `--with-deps` only when running in CI (`process.env.CI`) or on macOS/Windows (`os.platform() === 'darwin' | 'win32'`) — officially supported platforms where it works reliably. Omit it on other platforms (Linux) to avoid the `sudo` prompt. After a successful install without `--with-deps`, a formatted warning is printed informing users they may need to install additional OS libraries for Playwright to work correctly, directing them to run Storybook Test in the Storybook UI to identify missing dependencies, and showing the manual `--with-deps` command. Updated JSDoc to reflect the conditional behavior.
- **`postinstall.ts`**: Update the skipped-install warning to be platform-aware: shows `npx playwright install chromium --with-deps` on macOS/Windows, and `npx playwright install chromium` with an appended note pointing Debian/Ubuntu users to add `--with-deps` on other Linux platforms.
- **`AddonVitestService.test.ts`**: Update assertions to cover all code paths: CI (with `--with-deps`), Linux non-CI (without `--with-deps`), macOS/Windows (with `--with-deps`), and the post-install warning on Linux.

```diff
- const playwrightCommand = ['playwright', 'install', 'chromium', '--with-deps'];
+ const platform = os.platform();
+ const useWithDeps = !!process.env.CI || platform === 'darwin' || platform === 'win32';
+ const playwrightCommand = useWithDeps
+   ? ['playwright', 'install', 'chromium', '--with-deps']
+   : ['playwright', 'install', 'chromium'];
```

Without `--with-deps` on Linux local installs, Playwright downloads the Chromium binary only, skipping OS-level dependency installation. Browser dependencies are typically already present on Linux systems via the distro package manager. On macOS, Windows, and in CI environments, `--with-deps` is retained to ensure all required system dependencies are installed. On Linux, users are shown a post-install warning with guidance on how to check for and install any missing dependencies.

*This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

<issue_title>[Bug]: Storybook init can require `sudo` because of Playwright install</issue_title>
<issue_description>### Describe the bug

When initting Storybook and getting addon-vitest, the addon's postinstall installs Playwright _with dependencies_: 

https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/bd03a61573cbb1fc79bda8663ccdbc443ca22eda/code/addons/vitest/src/postinstall.ts#L294-L297

This can lead to the terminal require `sudo`, because that can be necessary to install the browser dependencies. This requirement can scare some users off, because they are not just giving `sudo` to the playwright install, but _to the whole init process_, which is opaque to the user and less secure.

### Additional context

Originally reported by @dominikg. I have not myself been able to reproduce this, it seems like Playwright refuses to install browsers on my machine, relying on some cached installs that I can't remove.

This the log shown:

```
› Configuring Playwright with Chromium (this might take some time):
  npx playwright install chromium --with-deps
[sudo] password for USER: 
```

If we don't add `--with-deps` it just downloads the binaries without using `sudo`. The deps are usually present from the system installed chromium and managed by the packaging system of the linux distro. It can lead to issues if the system installed chromium has deps that are incompatible from the one playwright wants to use, but that might not be an issue in practice.</issue_description>

## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section)

<comments>
<comment_new><author>@Sidnioulz</author><body>
I want to add to this that some commands, like `yarn start` in the monorepo, run install commands in quiet mode, so users don't even know it's Playwright asking for a password.

Besides, Playwright fails install on many Linux distros, and it tries for those distros to serve a 5 year old APT package for Ubuntu, which of course fails (all the package's dependencies have had multiple updates since then).

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/26482#issuecomment-2536547104 provides a command which apparently installs browsers without triggering this whole package download and sudo request. We might want to look into adding that `--shell-only` command if it has no relevant side effects for us.</body></comment_new>
<comment_new><author>@Sidnioulz</author><body>
> it's `--only-shell` https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli#install-browsers
> 
> i think you can only run headless tests then. might work for repo internal ci scripts but not user facing scripts as users might want to execute with browser ui showing

Thanks @dominikg! I suspect this might be enough for Addon Vitest, as it runs in CLI and outputs results in the UI and/or CLI. Let's see if the team believe --headed must be available by default.</body></comment_new>
<comment_new><author>@Sidnioulz</author><body>
Just tested rewriting addon-vitest's postinstall and `sudo` will keep being triggered until `--with-deps` is removed. Now, on my Arch system I can install with `--only-shell` and without `--with-deps`, and the addon runs fine because I already have playwright locally installed.

Obviously this means users without playwright will run into trouble.

One thing we could possibly do is use `execa` to run `playwright --version` and check if it's already installed; in which case `--with-deps` is redundant on Linux.

We could also try and detect distros. Playwright only supports Debian/Ubuntu so that shouldn't be too much of a stretch. [Plenty of options](https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/35183/how-do-i-identify-which-linux-distro-is-running) to detect distros.

ANd if we figure out that users do need to install Playwright themselves, provide a big fat visible warning for them so they know they have to do it.</body></comment_new>
<comment_new><author>@Sidnioulz</author><body>
> even though theg claim it only works w debian/ubuntu i haven't run into native issues with it on arch (manjaro) for years

Agreed, it's the NPM install DX that's broken. They don't know how to install it so they prompt you into typing a password and start downloading an Ubuntu 20 package, then they cry wolf because the package is using different dependency versions from the ones locally installed.

Meanwhile, not installing Playwright via NPM results in a functional experience for me on Arch.</body></comment_new>
<comment_new><author>@Sidnioulz</author><body>
Unfortunately it's not exactly the last step. It still does one or two things with Vitest config files afterwards.

@JReinhold, do you reckon it's doable to put the playwright install step at the very end of the process?

> I just installed Storybook and I really didn't like that it asked for a root password, because I don't know how it will affect my system. Does it install something using `pacman`? Does it install something in `/usr/bin`? I just pressed `Ctrl+C` and ...

</details>

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Environment variable restoration logic differs across tests.**

The `finally` blocks have inconsistent logic for restoring `process.env.CI`:
- Lines 443-447: Only restores if `originalCI !== undefined`
- Lines 502-508: Deletes if `originalCI === undefined`, else restores
- Lines 535-539: Only restores if `originalCI !== undefined`

Lines 443-447 and 535-539 may leave `process.env.CI` set if it was originally `undefined` but the test set it to a value. The pattern in lines 502-508 is correct.


<details>
<summary>🛠️ Suggested fix for consistent cleanup</summary>

```diff
       } finally {
-        if (originalCI !== undefined) {
-          process.env.CI = originalCI;
+        if (originalCI === undefined) {
+          delete process.env.CI;
+        } else {
+          process.env.CI = originalCI;
         }
       }
```

Apply this pattern to all three locations for consistency.
</details>


Also applies to: 502-508, 535-539

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/cli/AddonVitestService.test.ts` around lines 443 - 447, The
finally blocks currently restore process.env.CI inconsistently (some only
restore when originalCI !== undefined), which can leave CI set when it was
originally undefined; update all finally blocks in AddonVitestService.test.ts
that use originalCI/process.env.CI so they follow the correct pattern: if
originalCI === undefined then delete process.env.CI, else set process.env.CI =
originalCI. Locate uses of originalCI and the finally blocks around the tests
(the three spots shown around lines with the finally blocks) and apply this
consistent cleanup logic.
```

</details>
